the use of serum cystatin C as an alternative to creatinine for the estimation of the GFR is not as simple as it is often made out to be.
the GFR is the most important determinant of serum levels of cystatine C and creatinine.
cystatin C levels are affected not only by GFR, but also by age, gender, race, diabetes, C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, and serum albumin.

serum cystatin C is not a pure measure of GFR.
serum cystatin C is not a perfect surrogate marker of GFR and that other factors should be considered when using it as a marker of kidney function.
